title: The open storage bucket
brief: 18:30. A security researcher writes in: a file of Veltrix customer records is open to the whole internet, and a search engine has found it.
insight: Modelled on a pattern seen again and again: storage shared publicly “just to test”, forgotten, then indexed. The company here is fictional.
teaches: Take a good faith disclosure seriously: thank the researcher and act, do not threaten
Trace how it happened and how it was found, from the logs
Close the exposure, keep the evidence, and bring in data protection: it may be notifiable

script.say: Then it is a personal data breach, and the 72 hour clock may already be running. Close the link, but do not delete the file or the logs: we need them. Raise a ticket and I will take it from there.

mail.subject: Security issue: Veltrix customer data publicly accessible
body: I am an independent security researcher. While looking for exposed files I found a public Filebridge link on your account: customer_export_full.csv, about 41,000 rows of names, email addresses, phone numbers and delivery addresses.
It is indexed by Seekly, so anyone searching for your company can find it. I downloaded one copy to confirm what it was, and I have deleted it.
Please remove public access. I will not publish anything. I am happy to answer questions.

spf.explain: Sent by the researcher's own domain.

headers.summary: A genuine disclosure. No links, no attachments, and no demand for money.

replies.label: Reply: thank you, we are on it
replies.text: Thank you for telling us. We are removing access now, and our security team will follow up with you.

replies.label: Reply: delete everything or we call the police
replies.text: Delete everything you took immediately or we will involve the police.

outcome.label: Traced it in the audit log
outcome.what: Uploaded and shared with “anyone” in October 2025 “just to test”, indexed by a search engine in February, then downloaded by a script from the same address twice.
outcome.ideal: uses the logs to learn how the exposure happened and who reached the data.

outcome.label: Saw how anyone could find it
outcome.what: A search for the company name brings up the file. That is how the researcher found it, and how others did before her.
outcome.ideal: checks how an exposure is discoverable, not just that it exists.

outcome.label: Thanked the researcher
outcome.what: Good faith reporters are the cheapest early warning you will ever get. Treat them well.
outcome.ideal: acknowledges a good faith disclosure and hands it to security.

outcome.label: Brought in data protection
outcome.what: Nadia starts the breach assessment: 41,000 customers' details were public for eleven months.
outcome.ideal: involves data protection as soon as personal data is exposed.

outcome.label: Threatened the researcher
outcome.what: She told you about the problem for free. Threats make the next researcher publish instead of writing in.
outcome.ideal: thanks the reporter and lets security follow up.

investigate.objective: Confirm the exposure, trace how it happened, and close it.
investigate.insight: Most cloud exposures are not hacks. They are a setting someone chose “just to test” and nobody changed back.

hint.text: Search Seekly for “veltrix customer” to see what the researcher saw. In the Terminal, grep the Filebridge audit log for customer_export. Then open Filebridge and stop sharing the file. Call data protection on 4120.

outcome.label: Closed the public link
outcome.what: The file is no longer reachable. The logs and the file itself are kept for the investigation.
outcome.ideal: closes the exposure straight away and keeps the evidence.

card.title: Eleven months in public
body: The export was uploaded and shared with “anyone” in October 2025 as a test. A search engine indexed it in February. A script downloaded it twice in the last six weeks, before the researcher found it and told you.
You closed the link and kept the evidence. 41,000 customers' details were public, so this goes to data protection now: it may have to be reported within 72 hours.
card.ideal: closes it, traces it, and brings in data protection.

outcome.label: Limited the link to Veltrix staff
outcome.what: The public can no longer reach it, but a full customer export is still open to every employee. Nobody needs that.
outcome.ideal: stops sharing a file that nobody needs, rather than narrowing it.

report.objective: Raise it as a data incident.

hint.text: Raise a Helpdesk ticket: data exposed, shared or leaked.

outcome.label: Raised a data incident
outcome.what: Security and data protection can assess who downloaded it, and whether customers and the regulator must be told.
outcome.ideal: records a data exposure as an incident.
